subject: Re: Falken AI procurement — metrics access & temporary latency carveout
messages:
From: Holly Chen <holly.chen@falken.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@falken.ai, Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@falken.ai>
Date: 2026-09-17 09:12 -0700
Subject: Procurement questionnaire — measurement & dashboard access

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking our procurement packet. We're running through the SLO section and need a few clarifications before legal can sign off. High level asks below — can you reply with short answers and any artifacts? Our timeline is tight (sign by Sept 30).

1) How do you measure uptime and latency? Please describe the signal (synthetic probes, customer-facing telemetry, sampling rates) and the aggregation window for p95/p99.
2) What monitoring/alerting does a customer see vs what stays internal? Can we get read-only access to the production dashboards or a filtered view?
3) For noisy workloads where p95 spikes, do you offer a temporary exception path or remediation SLA? If so, what are the guardrails and escalation steps?
4) Any artifacts: measurement design, SOC 2 evidence summary, dashboard invite steps.

Also, we prefer attachments rather than long inline answers. Can you send an evidence packet and a single person we can follow up with?

Best,
Holly Chen
Head of Procurement
Falken AI

--
Holly Chen
Falken AI | procurement@falken.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Holly Chen <holly.chen@falken.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, procure@falken.ai
Date: 2026-09-17 11:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — measurement & dashboard access

Holly — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a short evidence packet and a measurement design doc (see attachments). Quick answers inline, full details in attached PDF (slo_measurement_design.pdf).

1) Measurement signal: we compute uptime from both synthetic probes (multi-region HTTP health checks every 30s) and production request telemetry (sampled at ~10% by default; configurable). Latency: customer-facing tail metrics are derived from per-request tracing (distributed traces + edge timings). Aggregation windows: rolling 5m windows for alerting, 1h windows for p95 reporting, 24h windows for monthly SLO calculation. p99 is computed on the same samples but we downsample to keep storage predictable; that is documented in the attachment.

2) Dashboard access: we provide read-only Grafana links scoped to the customer's tenant. By default customers get: uptime overview, p50/p95/p99 histograms, error-rate heatmaps, and recent incident traces. Sensitive internal signals (kernel-level host metrics, internal autoscaler traces, full raw sampling of every request) are redacted. We can create a filtered sampling stream if you need additional granularity for audit. Instructions to accept the invite are attached (grafana-invite-instructions.txt).

3) Temporary exception path: yes — we support a time-boxed SLO carveout (up to 14 days) for agreed regression events. Guardrails: request must include start/end, affected routes, mitigation plan, and rollback criteria. A carveout is logged in our procurement Jira and requires PM + Engineering sign-off. We will provide compensatory credits if the carveout was caused by our regression. Internal escalation flow is in the attachment and summarized below.

4) Artifacts attached: slo_measurement_design.pdf (design + sampling & aggregation), soc2-summary.pdf, grafana-invite-instructions.txt.

Point of contact: me (Sean Gallagher, account lead) and Marissa Cole (SRE lead, cc'd). If you want a quick walkthrough, propose 30 minutes and we'll send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: slo_measurement_design.pdf (PDF, 3 pages); soc2-summary.pdf (PDF, 2 pages); grafana-invite-instructions.txt (text)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-18 09:27 -07:00
Subject: internal: Falken carveout — approval path and quick notes

Sean — looping you and Priyom to confirm we can approve the 14-day carveout request pattern Holly asked about. Notes:

- Risk: providing a carveout for latency needs a mitigation plan; we should require reduced sampling and a rolling rollback test to prevent long-term regressions.
- Compensation: engineering recommends offering a 10% service credit for days where the agreed p95 gap exceeds the carveout threshold.
- Dashboard: we should provision Falken a filtered Grafana view that hides host-level metrics; attach the invite and retention controls.

If everyone agrees, I'll prepare the internal sign-off template and set the Jira ticket PROC-542 to "Ready for procurement". Sean — do you want to lead the customer-facing approval or should I?

Marissa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
